messages.content: "請您進行一個統計t檢定，以檢查兩個獨立數據集的平均值是否有統計上的差異？第一個數據集，數據集A，包含以下整數：12、15、18、20、22、25、28、30、32、35。第二個數據集，數據集B，包含以下整數：14、17、19、21、23、26、29、31、33、36。請分別以顯著性水平0.05和0.01進行兩次檢定。"

function.name: t_test
function.description: Perform a statistical t-test to check if the means of two independent datasets are statistically different. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

alpha.description: Significance level for the test. Default is 0.05. This is a float type value.

message.reasoning:
The user wants us to perform a statistical t-test on two independent data sets and provide results at alpha=0.05 and alpha=0.01.

We have tool "functions.t_test". We need to call it with dataset_A and dataset_B arrays. The default alpha is 0.05 but we can specify both tests separately or maybe run twice? They want separate significance levels; so likely do one test at alpha=0.05 then another at alpha=0.01. But the tool only accepts one alpha per invocation. So we will invoke twice: first with alpha=0.05, second with alpha=0.01.

But note: The tool returns some result (likely p-value etc). We'll just pass the arrays as numbers. Let's compute manually quickly:

Dataset A: [12,15,18,20,22,25,28,30,32,35]
Mean A = sum /10. Sum: 12+15=27, +18=45, +20=65, +22=87, +25=112, +28=140, +30=170, +32=202, +35=237. Mean = 23.7.

Variance A: Compute deviations squared:
(12-23.7)=-11.7^2=136.89
(15-23.7)= -8.7^2=75.69
(18-23.7)= -5.7^2=32.49
(20-23.7)= -3.7^2=13.69
(22-23.7)= -1.7^2=2.89
(25-23.7)=1.3^2=1.69
(28-23.7)=4.3^2=18.49
(30-23.7)=6.3^2=39.69
(32-23.7)=8.3^2=68.89
(35-23.7)=11.3^2=127.69
Sum squares: let's add: 136.89+75.69=212.58, +32.49=245.07,+13.69=258.76,+2.89=261.65,+1.69=263.34,+18.49=281.83,+39.69=321.52,+68.89=390.41,+127.69=518.10. Sample variance s² = 518.10/(n-1)=518.10/9≈57.5667. Standard deviation ≈ sqrt(57.567)=7.590.

Dataset B: [14,17,19,21,23,26,29,31,33,36]. Sum: 14+17=31, +19=50, +21=71, +23=94, +26=120, +29=149, +31=180, +33=213, +36=249. Wait double-check: Actually after adding 33 it's 213, plus 36 gives 249. Yes mean = 24.9.

Compute deviations squared:
14-24.9=-10.9^2=118.81
17-24.9=-7.9^2=62.41
19-24.9=-5.9^2=34.81
21-24.9=-3.9^2=15.21
23-24.9=-1.9^2=3.61
26-24.9=1.1^2=1.21
29-24.9=4.1^2=16.81
31-24.9=6.1^2=37.21
33-24.9=8.1^2=65.61
36-24.9=11.1^2=123.21
Sum squares: 118.81+62.41=181.22,+34.81=216.03,+15.21=231.24,+3.61=234.85,+1.21=236.06,+16.81=252.87,+37.21=290.08,+65.61=355.69,+123.21=478.90. Sample variance = 478.90/9=53.211... SD ~ sqrt(53.211)=7.295.

Now t-statistic formula for equal variances assumption? Usually use Welch's t-test because sample sizes same but variances differ slightly. Use pooled standard error: SE = sqrt(s1^2/n1 + s2^2/n2). n1=n2=10. So SE = sqrt((57.567)/10 + (53.211)/10 ) = sqrt(5.7567 + 5.3211) = sqrt(11.0778) = 3.328. Difference in means = 23.7 - 24.9 = -1.2. t = (-1.2)/SE = -0.3605 approx. Degrees freedom using Welch-Satterthwaite: df = ((s1^2/n1 + s2^2/n2)^2)/( (s1^2/n1)^2/(n1-1)+(s2^2/n2)^2/(n2-1)). Compute numerator: (5.7567+5.3211)^2 = (11.0778)^2 =122.78. Denominator: (5.7567^2)/(9)+ (5.3211^2)/(9). 5.7567^2=33.147, divide by9=3.681. 5.3211^2=28.332, div9=3.148. Sum denom=6.829. df=122.78/6.829=18.00 roughly. So degrees of freedom about 18.

p-value two-tailed from t distribution with df~18: For |t|=0.361, p > .70. So not significant at either alpha.

Thus output should state no difference found.

We'll produce JSON with results including t statistic, df, p-value, conclusion at each alpha.

Let's call tool once with alpha=0.05 and again with alpha=0.01. Provide outputs accordingly.
